## Natural history notes

A large metallic wood-boring beetle characterized by a flattened, elongated body, dark bronzy to black coloration, and deeply sculptured ridges on the wing covers. In Florida, the Sculptured Pine Borer is found in pine flatwoods, sandhills, pine forests, forest edges, and areas with dead, dying, or recently cut pine wood. Adults are often seen on pine logs, trunks, or at lights, while the larvae tunnel beneath bark and into pine wood, helping break down dead or weakened trees and supporting predators such as woodpeckers, parasitic wasps, and other forest insects.
